To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the call centre is not a new type of workplace, but a new way of organizing work.

(1) the majority of call centre workers do not experience high levels of work intensification, (2) the minority who do experience it are more likely to be female and/or part-time, (3) the majority of workers are dissatisfied with their work, (4) the minority who are satisfied are more likely to work in call centres with high levels of work intensity, (5) there are no significant differences between full- and part-time workers in terms of their levels of satisfaction,

the call centre industry has been a major source of employment growth in the UK, and that the call centre workforce has become more diverse in terms of age, gender, ethnicity, and educational attainment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which trade unions have attempted to respond to the new forms of work organization that have been established in the financial sector call centres that we studied.
the nature of work in the call centre industry, the role of trade unions in the industry, and the implications of these for the future of work.
the impact of call centres upon the lives and working conditions of their employees, and the implications of this for the future of work and trade unionism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the call centre sector is not homogeneous and that the call centre industry has been subject to a number of different forms of control and management.
the call centre is an environment in which the employee is under constant pressure to perform and to do so at a level that is beyond their capabilities.
the call center industry is not a good place for workers to work in.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new frontier of control in the call centre is the point of production, where the employee and the client interact.
we are trying to understand the nature of the relationship between work and employment and to identify how this can best be improved.
we have shown that call centres have been the site of a major transformation in the organisation of work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have to do more work on the front line of the call center, and we need to do that work with the workers who are there.
the call centre is a site of work that has become increasingly diverse in terms of the types of work that is done, and the types of employees that are employed.
there is a need for unions to focus on improving the work experience for employees, and to develop new forms of union organisation that can help workers to do this.
